name: Mandelbrot
summary: Render the Mandelbrot set as an N×N binary PBM bitmap, one bit per pixel.

spec.description: The Computer Language Benchmarks Game fractal, sequential, with the arithmetic order fixed so every language produces the same bits. Up to 50 iterations of z = z² + c per pixel: this measures scalar double-precision multiply/add throughput, tight branchy loops and bit packing.
spec.input: Exactly one argument N made only of ASCII digits (leading zeros allowed), with 1 ≤ N ≤ 16000; the image is N × N pixels.
spec.output: A binary PBM (P4) image: the ASCII header P4\n{N} {N}\n, then N rows from top (y = 0) to bottom, each ceil(N/8) bytes holding one bit per pixel from left (x = 0) to right, most significant bit first, padded with zero bits to a whole byte. A bit is 1 when the pixel stays in the set. Exit code 0.
rules: All arithmetic in IEEE-754 double precision, evaluated left to right exactly as written: cr = 2.0*x/N - 1.5 and ci = 2.0*y/N - 1.0.
Start with zr = zi = tr = ti = 0.0; up to 50 times, while tr + ti <= 4.0: zi = 2.0*zr*zi + ci; zr = tr - ti + cr; tr = zr*zr; ti = zi*zi. The pixel is in the set when tr + ti <= 4.0 afterwards.
Every operation is rounded on its own: no fused multiply-add, no complex-number types (they change the operation order), no cardioid/bulb or periodicity shortcuts, no hand-written SIMD, no threads.
Missing or extra arguments, non-digit characters, N = 0 or N > 16000: usage message on stderr, nothing on stdout, exit code 1.

benchmarks.description: N = 200 (5 KB of output): 40,000 pixels and about 1 million iterations, so process and runtime startup still weigh as much as the floating-point work.
N = 1000 (125 KB of output): one million pixels and about 24 million iterations of double-precision multiply/add, so the floating-point inner loop dominates.
